fit: oral mustard rice and short-term whole-saliva collection in healthy volunteers
assessment: Author abstract reports approximately fourfold fasting secretion with mustard rice versus threefold with unspiced rice in five participants. Exact mustard form and Parkinson drooling outcomes are unavailable.

fit: unstimulated salivary flow in Parkinson disease without a food intervention
assessment: Parkinson participants had reduced unstimulated secretion compared with matched controls. Salivary flow and patient complaints about excess saliva do not provide a food-specific drooling result.

fit: suspected injected rice-bran oil and acute altered consciousness
assessment: Single acute fat embolism case describes apathetic consciousness. Injected material identity and refining are unconfirmed. Clinical Parkinson apathy after food oil was not measured.

fit: pomegranate extract rinse and saliva chemistry in healthy adults
assessment: Salivary protein and enzyme outcomes changed. No raw aril exposure or clinical drooling outcome.

fit: oat milk-associated acute allergy and dysphonia
assessment: Case records acute dysphonia with laryngeal allergy after oat milk. Loudness, ordinary rolled oat consumption and Parkinson disease were not studied.

fit: injected thyme extract in a rat brain ischemia balance test
assessment: Two extract doses improved rotarod balance in the reported comparison. No dried culinary leaf, oral exposure or Parkinson postural-instability assessment.

fit: combined astaxanthin plus sesamin supplement with human attention subtests
assessment: Small per-protocol pilot reported differences in speed measures. Descriptive attention means did not favor the supplement at 12 weeks, with no inferential attention finding, separate sesamin arm or toasted oil.

fit: sesame oil cake solid-residue extract in a memory trial
assessment: Memory trial reports verbal learning effects and states that attention was not assessed. The extract is separate from edible sesame oil.

fit: medicinal Rhus javanica galls and exploratory attention measures
assessment: ASRS and Tower of Hanoi time favored the gall extract. Number count outcomes were inconclusive. Species, plant part, preparation and population differ from the frozen claim.

fit: isolated sesamol and rat-pup open-field or maze behavior
assessment: Isolated constituent improved several behaviors in a juvenile MSG exposure model. Mixed behavioral tests do not establish clinical attention after culinary toasted oil.

fit: acute walnut oil milkshake and conditioned fear learning
assessment: Existing trial reports faster fear extinction in young volunteers, with pressing method unverified. Fear prediction and executive-function impairment are distinct endpoints.
